solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stage acts for family members coming later?

parts.note: a step is a stage in a process
to mum is to act in a mummers' play or dumb show, so mums means acts

explanation.surface: A theatre programme note asking which performances suit relatives arriving late.
explanation.walkthrough: To mum is an old verb for performing as a mummer, a masked player in a folk drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepmother joins a family through a later marriage, hence the question mark on members coming later.

clue.text: Betting on cat making big impression

parts.note: SP is starting price, the odds in betting
the cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip, a lash

explanation.surface: A gambler backing a feline that makes a splash.
explanation.walkthrough: Cat suggests a pet but is the whip.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a splash is to make a striking impression.

clue.text: Noble gong that can have a piercing ring?

definitions.text: that can have a piercing ring?

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
gong is British slang for a medal or honour, such as the OBE

explanation.surface: A lord's medal with a sharp ring, like a struck gong.
explanation.walkthrough: A piercing ring sounds like a loud noise; it is jewellery through a pierced earlobe. The OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: The ear lobe is the usual place for a pierced earring.

clue.text: When depressed, one stops listening

parts.note: sounds like low spirits, but means physically pressed down
a device that, when pushed, prevents others hearing you

explanation.walkthrough: Depressed suggests a gloomy person tuning out; it is a key pressed on a phone or video call.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing this control on a phone cuts the microphone, so the other party no longer hears.

clue.text: I'm Norma — only, er, transformed …

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly admitting a change of identity.
explanation.walkthrough: Norma Jeane was her birth name; the star was transformed into a new persona, which the whole clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The actress was born Norma Jeane Mortenson and re-invented herself under a screen name.

clue.text: Jersey's sound? Mostly appealing, as are some blouses

parts.note: a Jersey is a breed of cow, and a cow's sound is a low

indicators.note: mostly means the word is used minus its final letter

parts.note: cute means charming or appealing

explanation.surface: Comment on a cardigan-like jersey and a tempting blouse in a fashion column.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey looks like a sweater but is the dairy cow from the Channel Island, whose moo is called a low.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-cut blouse has a neckline cut deep, a common style for such garments.

clue.text: Old police, rising before judge, depart

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: to be up is to appear in court before a judge
go means leave, depart

explanation.surface: An old policeman stands up in court, then leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The OGPU was the Soviet secret police of the 1920s and 30s.
explanation.definitionFit: This Soviet state security force preceded the NKVD and KGB, so an old police organisation.

clue.text: Tweet in which chapter welcome bishop to London?

parts.note: hi is a greeting, a welcome
RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title
going up to London is the British phrase for travelling to the capital

explanation.surface: A cathedral chapter greeting a bishop arriving in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Chapter suggests a cathedral body; here it only supplies its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A chirrup is a bird's short chirping call, a tweet.

clue.text: Television screening goddess in French poem

indicators.note: screening means shielding or enclosing, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: Hera is the Greek queen of the gods
en is French for in

explanation.surface: A television showing of a goddess in a French poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Screening suggests broadcasting, apt beside television, but it means hiding inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Raven is Edgar Allan Poe's famous narrative poem.

clue.text: My knowledge may be understood

indicators.note: understood here means heard, so the word for knowledge is taken by its sound

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: A modest claim that one's learning will be grasped by others.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the exclamation and the word for knowledge sound identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Lor is a dated exclamation of surprise, a clipped form of Lord, just like the interjection 'My!'.

clue.text: Recognition for work with screwdriver, say, and lever

parts.note: a screwdriver is an example of something that turns, a turner
to prize (or prise) is to lever something open

explanation.surface: Praise for a job done with simple tools from the toolbox.
explanation.walkthrough: The Turner Prize is Britain's best-known annual award for contemporary art.
explanation.definitionFit: The award honours an artist's work, so it is recognition for an artwork.

clue.text: Authoress with a last letter and article to follow spy novel

indicators.note: to follow puts the following pieces after the first

parts.note: to spy is to eye
Doris Lessing, Nobel-winning novelist
taken as written
Z is the last letter of the alphabet
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A writer with a final letter and essay following a spy thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: Spy novel looks like a genre; spy is the verb eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeless in Gaza is Aldous Huxley's 1936 book, a novel.

clue.text: Was ballooning attacked as winter sport?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: grew rapidly, as a snowball rolling downhill does
second meaning: pelted with snowballs in a playful winter fight

explanation.walkthrough: Ballooning suggests hot-air flights; here it means swelling fast, one sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to escalate quickly and literally to throw packed snow at someone.

clue.text: Song from a show recalled

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: to air is to show or broadcast
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tune remembered from a theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: Show looks like a noun for a musical but is the verb air.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera or oratorio.

clue.text: Left large hint, puzzled? The light may dawn on one!

definitions.text: The light may dawn on one!

indicators.note: puzzled means confused, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A solver left a big clue and is still baffled; illumination might come.
explanation.walkthrough: The light dawning sounds like understanding a clue; it is literal daybreak after a night without sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-nighter is a night spent awake, so morning daylight arrives during it.

clue.text: Old scientist not familiar with fashion

parts.note: something new is not yet familiar
ton is an old word for fashion or style, as in bon ton

explanation.surface: A historic scientist who never kept up with trends.
explanation.walkthrough: Ton for fashion is a crossword staple from French.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton was the seventeenth-century physicist, so an old scientist by any measure.

clue.text: Cheek, if not round, then oval

indicators.note: round means the other word goes around this one

parts.note: else means otherwise, if not
lip means impudent talk, cheek

explanation.surface: Describing a face: a cheek that is not circular must be egg-shaped.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheek looks like part of the face but means sauciness.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipse is the geometric figure loosely called an oval.

clue.text: Wretched defendant accepting tip from lawyer

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: the accused is the defendant in a trial

indicators.note: the tip of a word here is its end

parts.note: the tip of lawyer is its final letter

explanation.surface: A miserable defendant takes advice from counsel.
explanation.walkthrough: Tip suggests advice; it is the end letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Accursed means doomed or hateful, a sense of wretched.

clue.text: Who benefits from one visiting inexperienced youngster on round?

indicators.note: visiting means calling in on, so one letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: a cub is a novice, as in cub reporter
taken as written
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Asking who gains when somebody calls on a novice doing rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Cui bono is the Latin question 'to whose benefit?', used when looking for a motive.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase asks whose advantage something serves, the same question translated.

clue.text: What's now concealed by labyrinth, ingeniously

indicators.note: concealed by means the answer sits inside these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of labyrinth into the start of ingeniously

explanation.surface: Something modern cleverly hidden in a maze.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The in-thing is whatever is currently fashionable.

clue.text: Be absorbed with crime, and blood?

parts.note: sin is a wrongdoing, loosely a crime
blood means family, kin, as in blood relations

explanation.surface: A grim thriller about getting caught up in wrongdoing and bloodshed.
explanation.walkthrough: Blood looks like gore but means relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: When a fact sinks in it is fully taken in, absorbed by the mind.

clue.text: Drink often preceded by one very similar element

indicators.note: preceded by puts the following pieces ahead

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
to tope is to drink alcohol habitually

explanation.surface: A regular drinker's habit is preceded by a similar one.
explanation.walkthrough: Element sounds generic, but an isotope is a form of a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotopes are atoms of the same element differing only in neutron count, so closely alike.

clue.text: Brief mistrust minister's up against

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from the bottom, reversed

parts.note: sus is short for suspicion
a reverend is a minister; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A short-lived doubt about the vicar is aroused.
explanation.walkthrough: Brief suggests a moment; it signals a shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: Versus is Latin for against, used in sport and law.

clue.text: Capable of working at till

explanation.walkthrough: Till looks like a cash register, but it is the preposition meaning until.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers ability, current activity and a time limit, three separate everyday senses.

clue.text: Winger's worn green boots

indicators.note: worn suggests being battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: these ten letters are exactly those of the bird's name

explanation.surface: A footballer playing on the wing wears green boots.
explanation.walkthrough: Winger suggests a wide player in football; here it is anything with wings, a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The brent goose is a small dark wild bird, so a creature with wings.

clue.text: At least a dozen answer, giving endorsement

parts.note: VIs are sixes in Roman numerals, and two or more sixes make at least a dozen

explanation.surface: Twelve or more replies are given approval.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural of the Roman six makes at least twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official stamp in a passport, an endorsement permitting entry.

clue.text: I'd accept us going out together with one?

definitions.text: I'd accept us going out together with one?

indicators.note: going out together read as stepping out of line as a group, so all these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I, added on with

explanation.surface: A sweetheart agreeing to date, with a dark second reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Going out sounds like dating; read again it means dying together, which the whole clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A suicide pact is an agreement by two people to die at the same time.

clue.text: Passes on kiss every so often

indicators.note: every so often means only some letters are used, here every other one

parts.note: taking the first, third and fifth letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone forwards an occasional kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: Passes looks like a verb; it is the noun for approvals.
explanation.definitionFit: OKs are approvals, so things given a pass.

clue.text: Party outfit one turned down in work

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
gear is clothing, an outfit

explanation.surface: A party costume that one guest rejected while at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Turned down suggests refusing; it means a page corner folded over in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-ear is a folded corner of a page in a book, a written work.

clue.text: Beauty of headland, at first light

indicators.note: at first places this piece ahead of the other

parts.note: fair means light in colour, as hair or skin
a ness is a promontory, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Admiring a coastal cape at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: First light suggests dawn; at first is the order signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairness is an old word for loveliness, physical beauty.
